bugs_found: apply_fee uses 'fee <= fmin' which forces fee to fmin even when computed fee is already greater than fmin (boundary), and more importantly the comment 'bug' confirms an off-by-comparison: should be 'fee < fmin'
compound_interest does not validate principal can be negative (no check on p<0) which may produce nonsensical results
loan_payment returns p/m when r==0 but does not coerce to Decimal division precision context; acceptable but lacks rounding policy for monetary output
transfer mutates balances non-atomically without a lock/transaction; concurrent callers could double-spend
apply_fee/compound_interest/loan_payment/fx_convert lack explicit Decimal quantization/rounding to currency precision (e.g., 2 decimal places), risking sub-cent drift in financial outputs
fx_convert accepts rate from dict without validating rate>0, allowing zero/negative rates to silently produce wrong values
Account/Receipt dataclasses are mutable and have no validation (e.g., negative initial balance, empty id, invalid currency code)
No type hints on public functions reduces static-analysis safety in a financial module
